subject: Ember POC: integration next steps — quota, retries, request-id guidance
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@ember.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@ember.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.r@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ember POC recap + ask: load profile, auth preference, next call

Thanks for the call today — good discussion. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can start the PoC design: 

Summary
- Goal: 4-week PoC integrating Redwood inference for smart-replies + reranker for search results.
- Primary concerns: auth model, rate/quota expectations, 429/retry behaviour, and embeddings storage.

Technical follow-ups (what we need from Ember)
1) Production-ish load profile (qps, avg tokens per request, burst behaviour) — please send as CSV.
2) Preferred auth: API key or OIDC client? If OIDC, provide issuer + redirect metadata.
3) Any data residency constraints (EU-only data?) — you said US for now.

Initial Redwood recommendations (high level)
- SDK setup: client-side has API key with short TTL; recommend using our SDK's connection pooling default.
- Routing: route traffic to us-east for latency; we can pin to a Dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
- Embeddings/reranker: precompute embeddings for catalog; use approximate neighbor index + a lightweight reranker on Redwood for scoring.
- Rate limiting: token-based quotas with a per-minute burst allowance; on 429 we recommend exponential backoff + jitter and an idempotency key for user-visible actions.

Next steps
- Lena/Tom: drop the load_profile.csv (attachment suggested) and auth preference by EOD Friday.
- Camila (internal owner): will draft a minimal PoC plan (infra + cost estimate) and share Monday.
- Book a 30-min sync next Wed to finalize SLOs and rollout plan.

Attachments: suggested template ember-load-profile.csv (empty column headers in thread)

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ember POC recap + ask: load profile, auth preference, next call

Thanks Markus — nice write-up. Quick answers: 
- Load profile attached (ember-load-profile.csv). Expected steady-state: 18-22 rps for the search-rewrite endpoint; peaks up to ~120 rps for 90s during campaign spikes. Typical prompt size ~350 tokens; responses avg 80 tokens.
- Auth: we prefer OIDC for team SSO, but can use API keys for the PoC if that's simpler.
- Data residency: US only.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm recommended retry window & idempotency approach for reranker requests that update ranking logs? We need to avoid double-recording.
2) We want a fallback when quota throttles (e.g., degrade to cached top-N results) — can Redwood recommend a per-route fallback strategy?

We'll accept a quick design doc if Camila can provide it.

—Lena
Lena Ortiz
Head of ML — Ember.ai

From: Camila Reyes <camila.r@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@ember.ai>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@ember.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ember POC recap + ask: load profile, auth preference, next call

Hi Lena — thanks for the profile. Drafting two short docs and a checklist so you can evaluate quickly: 

Doc A: Retry/Idempotency summary (excerpt)- Retryable errors: 429, 502, 503, 504.
- Retries: client should implement limited exponential backoff (base=200ms, factor=2, maxAttempts=5) with full jitter.
- Request IDs: add X-Request-ID (UUID v4) per incoming user request that flows across retries. For mutating analytics (ranking logs) require an Idempotency-Key header derived from (user_id, session_id, action_hash).
- Server-side advice: Redwood will store a short-lived dedupe entry for Idempotency-Key (TTL = 24 hours) and return 409 if duplicate with same payload.

Doc B: Throttle & fallback strategy (excerpt)- Quotas: token-based per-tenant per-minute. Allow a 3x burst capacity for short spikes (<= 2 minutes) before returning 429.
- Graceful degradation: Offer cached top-N results client-side; call a smaller model (cheaper, faster) as fallback; or queue best-effort async rerank with eventual consistency.
- Observability: include token_consumption header in responses and a quota_remaining metric in the SDK.

I'll attach fuller notes (redwood-sdk-auth-routing-notes.pdf) to the Drive link. Action items: 
- Internal: Marissa will prepare the idempotency implementation plan and how it maps to our audit logs.
- External: Lena/Tom to confirm OIDC metadata or whether to proceed with API keys for PoC.

Camila
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

This is helpful. Two quick clarifications on idempotency: 
- We log ranking impressions in an event store; if Redwood returns 409 for duplicates, do you expose the original event id so we can reconcile?
- If retries are in flight, would you recommend client-side buffering with single-send (dedupe) or letting the SDK handle retries transparently?

For PoC speed, we'll go API key for the first week and switch to OIDC afterward.

Thanks,
Tom
Eng Lead — Ember.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@ember.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.r@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena@ember.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ember POC recap + ask: load profile, auth preference, next call

Tom — quick answers: 
- When we detect a duplicate Idempotency-Key we return 409 and include X-Original-Event-ID in the response headers (if the original produced an event). That header is available via the SDK as response.meta.original_event_id. That should help reconciliation.
- Recommended pattern: do client-side single-send for any event that must be unique (e.g., billing or impression writes). For user-facing generation calls, let the SDK handle retries transparently with request-id for tracing.

Implementation notes (high level)
- Idempotency-Key generation: use sha256(user_id + session_id + action_type + iso_ts_truncatedToMinute) to avoid accidental duplicates from concurrent clicks.
- Backoff tuning: base 250ms, factor 2, max 6 attempts, full jitter — this balances spike recovery with UX.
- Logging: we emit throttled_response_count and idempotency_conflict_count to per-tenant metrics that you can pull in the console.

I'll add a sample code snippet to the Drive doc for your engineers.

Marissa
Product Ops — Redwood Inference
